mentl/190b4b1:
Parser's handle-expr `with` clause was special-casing three forms (state-init,
effect-row, named-handler) via $parse_handler_state. The TIdent-not-TEq branch
called $skip_to_lbrace_p — correct for handler-decl context (where `{ ARMS }`
follows unconditionally) but silently consuming subsequent top-level fns when
used in handle-expr context with `handle BODY with NAME` form.

Substrate move: handler-value is just an expression (kernel primitive 2 —
handlers w/ typed resume). The graph + infer narrow what kind-of-handler
EXPR is at type-check time. Parser branches doing form-disambiguation are
the cursor-IS-the-substrate drift wearing parser-state clothes — drift mode
9 (deferred-by-omission) at the syntactic layer.

Eight interrogations:
  Graph?      install_expr is an NExpr handle in the same graph.
  Handler?    parse_handle_expr handler @resume=OneShot.
  Verb?       Implicit |> in token consumption.
  Row?        TokenRead effect; same as parse_expr.
  Ownership?  install_expr alloc'd by parse_expr; bump-owned.
  Refinement? parse_expr's contract returns a valid NExpr.
  Gradient?   Install resolution at infer-time (handler-as-value
              type-check); parse stays opaque.
  Reason?     install_expr's Reason chain reads back to TWith span.

Drift refused: 1 (no dispatch table); 6 (no primitive special-case —
EXPR uniform); 8 (structural kind peek); 9 (closes form-3 named
follow-up Hβ.first-light.handle-expr-with-named-handler-substrate).

Two forms for handle-expr's with-clause:
  with FIELD = INIT, ...   — anon-handler state-init (form 2)
  with EXPR                — handler install (form 3)
Disambiguation: peek past TWith.
  TIdent followed by TEq → state-init field-loop
  anything else          → parse_expr

HandleExpr AST grows install_expr at offset 16 (additive — older readers
of body/arms/state stay correct).

Empirical:
  handle_const fixture: 3 fn defs → 6 fn defs (all sibling fns now
    parsed; previously absorbed into handle-expr's arms).

mentl/19807fb:
Phase 1 rewritten from flat checklist to dependency cascade.
Each step depends on the one before it, empowers the one after:

  1. types.jxj     → bedrock (every file imports this)
  2. graph.jxj     → substrate (everything reads the graph)
  3. effects.jxj   → algebra (inference needs row ops)
  4. infer.jxj     → engine (writes into graph + env)
  5. env_handler   → state (inference needs env to run)
  6. lower.jxj     → observer (reads post-inference graph)
  7. pipeline.jxj  → spine (assembles all components via ~>)
  8. emit.jxj      → output (LowIR → WAT)
  9. memory.jxj    → runtime (compiled code calls into)
  10. main.jxj     → entry (the compiler is a binary)
  11. error catalog → mentorship (every code has docs)
  12. integration   → proof (inka query + exit gate tests)

Every step names its dependencies, what it unlocks, formatting
requirements, and exit criteria. No step is skippable or reorderable.
mentl/19cdd88:
effect Iterate { yield(element), result() }. iterate(xs) yields each element. Every collection operation is a handler: map transforms on yield, filter gates on yield, fold accumulates on yield, take counts on yield. Same effect, different handlers. result() extracts handler state.

Stream fusion falls out: compose handlers on the same iterate, one pass, no intermediates. Fan-out ready: xs <| (map(f), filter(p), fold(g, 0)) — three handlers, three results.

Also: FanOutExpr in codegen.lux + lower.lux (was missing). compile_wasm_fast deleted (checker not optional). Dead type_map code removed from emitter + pipeline.

27 benchmark tests pass. Full backward compat — same function signatures, effect-based internals.
